header.running_head: Who is Most Worthy of Assuming the Office of Khilaafah

Hadhrat Sufyaan bin Abi Awjaa narrates that Hadhrat Umar bin Khattaab (RA) once said, "By Allaah! I know not whether I am a Khalifah or a king. If I am a king, then the matter is serious indeed." Someone from the audience said, "O Ameerul Mu'mineen! There is a distinct difference between the two. A Khalifah only takes something rightfully and then uses it rightfully. By the grace of Allaah, you are exactly like this. On the other hand, a king oppresses people by usurping things from some and then giving them to others." Hadhrat Umar (RA) remained silent. [^2]

Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) reports that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once asked them, "Am I a king or a Khalifah?" Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) replied, "If you had ever (unlawfully) taken even a Dirham or less from the property of the Muslims and then used it illegally, you would be a king and not a Khalifah." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then began to weep bitterly. [^3]

A man from the Banu Asad tribe narrates that he was present when Hadhrat Umar (RA) once addressed his companions. Amongst them was Hadhrat Talha (RA), Hadhrat Salmaan (RA), Hadhrat Zubayr (RA) and Hadhrat Ka'b (RA). He said to them, "I want to ask you something. However, you should beware not to lie to me because you would then destroy me as well as yourselves. I ask you to tell me in the name of Allaah whether I am a Khalifah or a king." Hadhrat Talha (RA) and Hadhrat Zubayr (RA) said, "You are asking us something that we have no knowledge of. We are unable to distinguish a Khalifah from a king." Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) then testified with full conviction that Hadhrat Umar (RA) was a Khalifah and not a king. Hadhrat Umar (RA) responded by saying, "You have a right to comment because you had been frequenting the company of Rasulullaah ﷺ." Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) then qualified his statement by saying, "I say this because you exercise justice amongst your subjects, you distribute between them with fairness, you treat them with the compassion that a man treats his own family and you pass judgement according to the Book of Allaah."
Hadhrat Ka'b (RA) then said, "I was under the impression that none in this gathering besides me could differentiate between a king and a Khalifah. However, it is evident that Allaah has filled Salmaan with wisdom and knowledge." Hadhrat Ka'b (RA) then addressed Hadhrat Umar (RA) saying, "I testify that you are definitely a Khalifah and not a king." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then asked, "How is this?" Hadhrat Ka'b (RA) (who had been scholar of the previous scriptures) replied, "I have found mention of you in Allaah's scriptures." "Was mention made of me by my name?" enquired Hadhrat Umar (RA). "No," replied Hadhrat Ka'b (RA), "but I have found mention of you by your qualities. I
